question: How does TCS describe its strategy around AI services and partnerships? (FY2026)
answer:
TCS's AI strategy is guided by the aspiration to become the world's largest AI-led technology services company by providing full-stack AI solutions from infrastructure to intelligence [TCS FY2026 p.55] [TCS FY2026 p.1]. The company is repositioning as an AI and digital transformation partner by embedding AI across its service portfolio through a 'Human+AI' service autonomy model and an industry-specific agent marketplace [TCS FY2026 p.9] [TCS FY2026 p.7]. Its transformation agenda is structured around five strategic pillars: internal transformation, redefining services, building a future-ready talent model, enabling AI adoption for clients via an 'Innovate–Build–Scale with AI' playbook, and strengthening its AI ecosystem play [TCS FY2026 p.55] [TCS FY2026 p.3].

For partnerships, TCS aims to act as an integrator and orchestrator across the AI stack, extending beyond traditional implementation roles through strategic collaborations, shared investment models, and inorganic acquisitions [TCS FY2026 p.1] [TCS FY2026 p.58]. Key initiatives include launching the HyperVault AI infrastructure platform in partnership with TPG and OpenAI [TCS FY2026 p.1] [TCS FY2026 p.58], deepening collaborations with hyperscalers, chipmakers, and software providers (such as AMD, OpenAI, Google Cloud, ServiceNow, and others) [TCS FY2026 p.3] [TCS FY2026 p.58], and acquiring firms like Coastal Cloud and ListEngage to expand Salesforce and agentic AI consulting capabilities [TCS FY2026 p.1] [TCS FY2026 p.3].

question: What progress does Reliance report on its new energy giga-factories? (FY2026)
answer:
At the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex in Jamnagar, Reliance reported the following progress on its giga-factories in FY2025-26:

• Solar PV Manufacturing: Core manufacturing assets were commissioned and Phase I became operational [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54]. The company successfully produced its first 200 MWp of heterojunction (HJT) modules (720 Wp BIS-certified panels) [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54, p.58], and capacity ramp-up is underway to scale to 10 GWp per annum, with a planned expansion to 20 GWp [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54, p.58]. Polysilicon, glass, ingots, and wafers are being commissioned in phases toward full integration [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54].

• Battery Energy Storage (BESS): The battery giga-factory is in advanced commissioning and on track to commission in phases in 2026-27 [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54, p.58]. Civil construction is complete and equipment installation is underway, with production ramping through the second half of 2026 (focusing on LFP chemistry) to initially deliver 40 GWh of annual capacity, scalable to 100 GWh [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54, p.58].

• Electrolysers: Reliance secured an exclusive technology licensing agreement from Nel ASA for alkaline electrolysers in India, has started work on setting up the electrolyser giga-factory, and plans to commission and ramp up the facility in phases over coming quarters, with capacity scalable up to 3 GW per year [RELIANCE FY2026 p.54, p.58].

question: What happened with the demerger of ITC's hotels business? (FY2025)
answer: The demerger of ITC's Hotels Business into ITC Hotels Limited (ITCHL) under a Scheme of Arrangement was approved by shareholders on June 6, 2024, and by the NCLT Kolkata Bench on October 4, 2024, becoming effective on January 1, 2025 [ITC FY2025 p.151]. Under the Scheme, the Hotels Business (excluding ITC Grand Central, Mumbai) and hospitality investments/net assets were transferred to ITCHL on a going concern basis [ITC FY2025 p.209, p.314]. The carrying/book value of transferred net assets was ‣ 10,694.76 Crores on a standalone basis [ITC FY2025 p.209] and ‣ 10,466.83 Crores on a consolidated basis [ITC FY2025 p.314]. On January 11, 2025, ITCHL allotted 125,11,71,040 Equity Shares of ‣ 1/- each to ITC's shareholders (as of record date January 6, 2025) [ITC FY2025 p.209, p.314]. Consequently, ITCHL ceased to be a subsidiary and became an associate of ITC (with ITC retaining a 39.88% shareholding), and other hospitality subsidiaries, joint ventures, and associates ceased to hold those respective statuses [ITC FY2025 p.151, p.209].

question: What is L&T's Lakshya strategic plan and what targets does it set? (FY2026)
answer: L&T's Lakshya strategic plan is a medium-term (5-year) integrated planning framework that sets long-term goals, guides capital allocation, and identifies enterprise growth opportunities, including Lakshya 2026 (concluded March 2026) and Lakshya 2031 (FY27–FY31) [LT FY2026 p.30, p.34]. Strategic objectives and targets set under these plans include: Lakshya 2031 Objectives & Targets: 1. Existing Businesses: Continue EPC and Manufacturing momentum with improved profitability, pursue selective geographical diversification in EPC, pivot LTM and LTTS to an AI-led operating model, and drive accelerated growth in Financial Services and Realty [LT FY2026 p.34]. 2. New Businesses: Position Green Hydrogen/Ammonia, Offshore/Onshore Wind, SuFin, Semiconductor, Industrial Electronics, and Larsen & Toubro Vyoma as 2030s growth engines with selective value unlocking [LT FY2026 p.34]. 3. Technology & Shareholder Value: Strengthen domain technology, extensively use AI/digital for operational efficiency, and increase shareholder value through improved profitability and return on capital deployed [LT FY2026 p.34]. 4. Portfolio & Operational Enablers: Establish Electronics Products and Systems (EPS) as a strategic deep-tech IP-led vertical [LT FY2026 p.32], deliver 2X improvement in workforce productivity, and build a strong leadership pipeline [LT FY2026 p.34]. 5. Natural Capital (by FY 2030-31): Plant 1.5–2 million saplings annually and reach Zero-Waste-to-Landfill status for all manufacturing facilities and 10% of EPC project sites in India [LT FY2026 p.226]. Lakshya 2026 Targets: Achieve a 30% reduction in emissions intensity and a 25% reduction in energy intensity by FY 2025-26 compared to the FY 2020-21 baseline [LT FY2026 p.226].

question: How does Airtel describe its 5G rollout and spectrum position? (FY2026)
answer:
Airtel describes its 5G rollout and spectrum position as follows:

**5G Rollout:**
- **Deployment & Architecture:** Airtel completed nationwide deployment of its 5G Standalone (SA) network, becoming the first domestic operator to maintain a dual-mode (SA+NSA) architecture [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.136, BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.54]. 
- **Migration:** FWA has been fully migrated to the SA network, while mobile customers are transitioning in a phased manner based on handset readiness [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.0, BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.51].
- **Site Expansion:** Deployed 35,499 5G sites to enhance data experience [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.136] and expanded its overall 5G footprint with over 10,450 new sites added [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.55].
- **Technology & Optimization:** Implemented network slicing with Fastlane technology for higher speeds and lower latency [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.136], and refarmed 4G spectrum (in 1800, 2100, and 2300 MHz bands) to extend 5G coverage and support accelerated 5G traffic migration [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.136, BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.54].

**Spectrum Position:**
- **Mid-Band Holdings:** Airtel holds India's largest and most diversified mid-band spectrum portfolio, comprising 352.45 MHz in the 1800 MHz band, 235 MHz in the 2100 MHz band, and 790 MHz in the 2300 MHz band [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.54].
- **Other Holdings:** Holds 166.6 MHz in the 900 MHz band, 20 MHz in the 800 MHz band, 2,200 MHz in the 3300 MHz band, and 18,000 MHz in the mmWave (26 GHz) band [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.54].
- **Spectrum Acquisition:** Entered into an agreement with Adani Data Networks Limited to acquire rights to 400 MHz of spectrum in the 26 GHz band across six states (Gujarat, Mumbai, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu) to support 5G expansion and future capacity needs [BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.37, BHARTIARTL FY2026 p.94].

question: What does Maruti say about its new manufacturing facility at Kharkhoda? (FY2026)
answer:
Maruti highlights several aspects regarding its greenfield manufacturing facility at Kharkhoda, Haryana:

- **Capacity and Timeline:** Production ramp-up activities progressed steadily during the year [MARUTI FY2026 p.149]. The facility is set to be commissioned / commence commercial production in FY 2026-27 with an annual capacity of 250,000 vehicles [MARUTI FY2026 p.144, p.149], and is designed with multi-powertrain flexibility [MARUTI FY2026 p.149].
- **Renewable Energy and Decarbonisation:** The plant transitioned to 100% renewable electricity as its primary power source in March 2026 [MARUTI FY2026 p.166] and currently operates on 100% renewable electricity [MARUTI FY2026 p.179]. A 1 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) was commissioned to support surplus solar utilisation and grid stability, estimated to reduce approximately 54 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually [MARUTI FY2026 p.50, p.179]. Additionally, a 10 TPD Compressed Biogas (CBG) plant is under construction and scheduled to be commissioned by 2027 [MARUTI FY2026 p.166].
- **Water Stewardship:** A rainwater-harvesting pond with a capacity of 3,13,000 KL was commissioned at the facility during FY 2025-26 [MARUTI FY2026 p.179].
- **Workforce Infrastructure:** Key workforce initiatives at the site include a dormitory facility with expansion plans for ~4,500 workers, Facial Recognition System attendance, commute shuttle vehicles, canteens, stores, an in-house SBI branch, and telecom towers [MARUTI FY2026 p.94].

question: What does Sun Pharma report about US FDA inspections of its facilities? (FY2025)
answer: Sun Pharma reports the following regarding US FDA inspections and regulatory actions at its facilities: Mohali Facility: Inspected by the US FDA in August 2022 and classified as Official Action Indicated (OAI) [SUNPHARMA FY2025 p.203, p.292]. In April 2023, the US FDA issued a Consent Decree Correspondence/Non-Compliance letter directing corrective actions before releasing finished drug product batches into the US, including retaining an independent cGMP expert for batch certifications [SUNPHARMA FY2025 p.203, p.292]. Dadra Facility: Inspected in December 2023 and classified as OAI [SUNPHARMA FY2025 p.203, p.292]. In June 2024, the US FDA issued a Warning Letter summarizing cGMP violations, and the company is taking corrective measures to achieve full compliance [SUNPHARMA FY2025 p.203, p.292]. Priorities: A top priority for FY26 is to enhance compliance across manufacturing operations and work towards full regulatory resolution at three facilities facing US FDA action [SUNPHARMA FY2025 p.12].
